biography: Ken Schraeder wasn't born into racing royalty. Growing up in rural Missouri, his first taste of speed came from fixing up old pickup trucks with his dad. The roar of an engine, the smell of gasoline – it was intoxicating. He started out on dirt tracks, hustling a beat-up Ford into the top five every week, his raw talent undeniable. A local sponsor, impressed by his tenacity, helped him move into the Stock USA Gen2 series. His breakthrough came at the Heartland Speedway, battling wheel-to-wheel with veteran racers, showcasing his composure under immense pressure, ultimately securing his first victory. Now, at 31, Ken is a force to be reckoned with, a steady presence in a sport known for its volatility, aiming for championship glory.
drivingStyle: Schraeder is a master of consistency and tire management. He doesn't overdrive the car, preferring a smooth, calculated approach. He meticulously analyzes the track, identifying the optimal line and conserving his tires for a late-race charge. He's known for his exceptional racecraft, often making daring overtakes in the closing laps, demonstrating a remarkable ability to handle pressure when the stakes are highest.

careerHighlight: Winning the Heartland Speedway race in his rookie season, proving he could compete with the best in the series and marking his arrival as a serious contender.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship decider at Riverside Raceway due to mechanical failure, costing him the title by a single point.
